title: Unify legacy token semantics and update controls usage examples
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Consolidate current token semantics (legacy: semantic.primary/secondary vs. new: surface/brand/neutral) and publish a clear, example-driven guide for engineers and designers that covers buttons, table rows/cells, and chart legend/axis color usage.

Why: We have drift between design token names used in Figma, the runtime token JSON, and the component APIs. This causes inconsistencies in color application (e.g., disabled states, hovered emphasis on tables) and makes it hard for engineers to adopt quantized palettes and the Optimize recommendations. The doc updates will: 1) define canonical token mapping, 2) provide migration snippets for codebases, 3) show do/don't visual examples, and 4) add a small API appendix for controls that references props and expected token inputs.

Deliverables:
- Token mapping table (legacy -> canonical -> platform key) as a downloadable JSON and CSV.
- Example patterns for Buttons (primary/secondary/ghost/disabled) with code snippets for React + Redwood SDK.
- Table styles guidelines: row emphasis, zebra vs. no-zebra, focus outlines, cell truncation rules.
- Charts legend/axis guidance: when to use semantic vs. neutral tokens, contrast targets for WCAG AA, and guidance for colorblind-safe palettes.
- Migration snippets and a checklist for engineers to reduce visual regressions.
- A short FAQ addressing runtime behavior (prefix caching, token overrides in Dedicated/Private deployments).

Acceptance criteria:
- PR to design-site merged with the token mapping page and example pages.
- Two sample app screenshots (before/after) present in the page.
- Sign-off from PM (Priya Kapoor) and Accessibility reviewer (Evan Li).
- Updater script (scripts/token-mapper.js) included in the repo with instructions in the doc.
